chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Husayn ibn Na'im, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
O Husayn, be generous with the grace. I said: May I be sacrificed for you, and what thing is generosity with it? He said: To attempt doing good with what remains to you.

key_terms.اصْطِنَاعُ الْمَعْرُوفِ: Doing good / performing acts of kindness

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of generosity towards divine grace according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the true gratitude for divine blessings not merely as acknowledgment, but as the active perpetuation of favor by using one's remaining resources to benefit others. This concept, known as *ihsan* (excellence in doing good), reflects the Shia understanding that the preservation of a blessing is contingent upon its circulation through charitable acts, thereby transforming personal wealth into a means of spiritual continuity.
